## Different machines -- Same story

A packaging line, a fed-batch bioreactor, a pharmaceutical freeze-dryer, etc.

The freeze-dryer, for instance. The pump load was drifting from batch 17 {{< iconify picon:rise >}}. The deviation hit at batch 50 {{<iconify si:bin-fill>}}.\
But the signal was there the whole time...

---

## Two types of signals

**Discrete events** <small>-- alarms on/off, valve open/closed, operator entries..., timestamped.</small>\
This is what audit trails are made of. That's what **machinelogR** reads.

**Continuous measurements** <small>-- temperature, pressure, weight... over time.</small>\
This is typically what historians store. That's what **processlogR** will handle.

Different data. Same logic. Two sister packages.

---

## Architecture

<img src="images/lego_bricks.jpg" style="float: right; margin-left: 1.5rem; margin-bottom: 1rem; width: 25%;" />

A few examples of functions:

`alarm_pareto()` counts alarm frequencies.\
`spc_chart()` plots a control chart.\
`lyo_batch()` simulates a freeze-drying batch.

A function, a simulator, and a [grammar rule](toolbox/machinelogr.html) are all **bricks**.\
Bricks snap together into **walls**. Walls build **houses** -- a CPV report, a maintenance dashboard, an audit trail review.\
{{< iconify lucide:toy-brick >}} → {{< iconify lucide:brick-wall >}} → {{< iconify lucide:house >}}

The same brick, like `spc_chart()`, may appear in different houses.\
The context changes. The function does not.



```{mermaid}
graph TD
    D1["<b>Discrete events</b><br/><small>alarms, states, entries...</small>"] --> M1["<b>machinelogR</b><br/><small>alarm_pareto(), spc_chart(), connect_fmea_to_log()...</small>"]
    D2["<b>Continuous measurements</b><br/><small>temperature, pressure, load...</small>"] --> M2["<b>processlogR</b><br/><small>lyo_batch()...</small>"]

    M1 --> P1["Part I -- <b>Pharma & GxP</b><br/><small>CPV · audit trail · FMEA · ...</small>"]
    M1 --> P2["Part II -- <b>Operations & I4.0/I5.0</b><br/><small>OEE analysis · predictive maintenance · ...</small>"]
    M2 --> P1
    M2 --> P2
```

## The datasets

All datasets used here are either open data or generated on this site.

**PIADE** (Packaging Industry Anomaly DEtection) is a real dataset -- packaging line logs published as open data on [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/orvile/packaging-industry-anomaly-detection-dataset). That's what I used to build and test **machinelogR** on actual industrial data.

**FDSim** is a freeze-dryer simulator I built for this site. You can explore it in the [Toolbox](toolbox/fdsim.html).

**IndPenSim** (Industrial-scale Penicillin Simulation) is a public simulator for fed-batch bioreactors ([industrialpenicillinsimulation.com](http://www.industrialpenicillinsimulation.com/)). I use it to build and validate **processlogR**, and as a showcase for continuous bioprocess data.

Real data from real plants exists. It won't appear here -- but the tools are built to read it.
